mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a high-inflation regime where real rates do not rise.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in Real Final Sales of Domestic Product (RSAFS) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 70% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when accompanied by simultaneous large fiscal stimulus.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly different from zero during triggered periods, or the effect reverses when wage growth accelerates.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the Industrial Production Index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% over three consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings visibility and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of strong export demand.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (CPI) above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual shock of higher interest rates and inflation, which erodes real purchasing power and compresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative during co-occurrence of these signals, or the effect reverses when GDP growth accelerates.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) below 900K units for four consecutive months signals a housing market downturn, which reduces construction-related economic activity and drags on equity returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of strong mortgage rate declines.

mechanism_narrative: A positive and accelerating trend in PAYEMS (nonfarm payrolls) growth over three consecutive months, combined with a stable unemployment rate, signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS 3-month YoY growth acceleration AND UNRATE flat (<0.1pp change)
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive during triggered periods, or the effect reverses when wage growth decelerates sharply.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent quarterly decline in real GDP (GDPC1) for two consecutive quarters signals a macroeconomic recession, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days regardless of other conditions.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative during two consecutive quarters of real GDP contraction, or the mechanism fails during war-driven demand shocks.
